description:
FOUND and FIXED s456ag (Opus agent AG, round 13) while clearing the cpan-`t`
census population.  Filed as a record: the two drops it removes had no task of
their own (they were the "WTF? :-) Expr starts with ->/brace??" rows in
Test-Simple's t/Legacy/Regression/637.t and
t/Test2/modules/API/InterceptResult.t).

THE SHAPE:

    sub intercept (&) { â¦ }        my $x = intercept { 5 }->upgrade;
    sub many (&;@)    { â¦ }        my $y = many { 5 }->n;

perl: `intercept(sub{â¦})->upgrade`.  The slurpy `@` of a block prototype
consumes JUXTAPOSED TERMS, and `->` cannot start a term -- it is a POSTFIX
operator that binds to the block call's RESULT.

WAS: Pl::PExpr's block-prototype branch ended the slurp only at `,` and `=>`
(`$comma_stops`), so `_take_rest_as_args` swallowed `-> upgrade` (and, at a
call site like `print "1 ", one { 5 }->upgrade, "\n"`, everything after it).
The `->` then arrived at the postfix handler as element 0 of an argument list,
where the die at Pl/PExpr.pm:1149 is the only honest answer.

NOW: `->` is a third stop, which leaves the arrow IN the token stream -- exactly
what `eval`/`do` already do (the note at the inline-lambda branch says so), and
the ordinary postfix machinery then binds it onto the funcall node.

PROBED vs perl 5.40.3, 11 shapes identical: `(&)` and `(&;@)` before a method,
a chain, `->[1]`, `->{k}`; and the inverses that must NOT change -- a juxtaposed
term is still slurped (`blk { 5 } 1, 2` = 3 args), a comma still ends the slurp
(`(many { 5 }, 1, 2)[0]`), a block call inside a list/arrayref/hash value.

MEASURED: corpus-diff IDENTICAL over 111; emission A/B vs 83b335f over the four
populations -- 637.t and InterceptResult.t the only files it moves, RCDIFF 0.
Guard Pl/t/method-name-word-01.t (5 block-form rows, 2 of them inverses).
subject: DONE s456ag: a `(&â¦)`-prototype BLOCK CALL ends at `->` -- `intercept {â¦}->upgrade` was swallowing the arrow into the slurpy argument list and dropping the statement ("WTF? :-) Expr starts with ->/brace??")
